meta: No test needed: let real users grade AI. Type a question, get two answers from two unnamed AIs, click the better one, and only then see the names. Each vote is like a chess game, scored with Elo.

muc.title: Let the users grade it
muc.text: Last time, we saw AI tests can leak. So let's drop the test and let the users be the judges.

muc.title: Two anonymous answers
muc.text: You type a question and get two answers from two unnamed AIs. After reading, you click the better one. Only then are the names shown.

muc.title: Chess-style scores
muc.text: Each vote is like a chess game: the winner gains points, the loser loses some. Beating a strong opponent earns more. This is called an Elo score, like chess player rankings.

muc.title: Millions of votes
muc.text: Add up millions of votes like this, and you get a leaderboard. The best-known site is LMArena, and anyone can try it.

muc.title: Close to real life
muc.text: The good part: the questions are real questions from real users, new every day, so it's very hard to cram for.

muc.title: Long and pretty isn't always right
muc.text: The downside: voters tend to prefer long, nicely formatted, confident answers. A short answer that's correct can sometimes lose.

muc.title: Run your own blind match
muc.text: You can do this yourself: ask two AIs the same question, copy both answers, and hide the names. Ask a coworker to pick the better one. Do a few questions, and you'll know which AI suits your work.

muc.title: Write your own test
muc.text: But a general leaderboard still isn't your work. Write your own test. See you in part 4.
